anticipation_heuristics.pre_cycle_gate: If the artifact is absent after repeated blockers, route to artifact_sprint, falsifier_sprint, demotion, or quarantine.
anticipation_heuristics.prompt_heuristic: Before proof search, ask: which concrete table, interval, bound, code output, or theorem must exist for this hypothesis to become live?
anticipation_heuristics.why_it_matters: A branch cannot move by reasoning alone when promotion depends on a named missing artifact.

anticipation_heuristics.pre_cycle_gate: Quarantine until same-domain transfer or same-theory carrier preservation is explicit.
anticipation_heuristics.prompt_heuristic: Ask whether the source object and target object remain in the same theory, regulator, observable family, and validity regime.
anticipation_heuristics.why_it_matters: A proof route can become easier by silently changing the object instead of solving the target problem.

anticipation_heuristics.pre_cycle_gate: Demote to support-only unless the next artifact directly tests a target-facing transfer gate.
anticipation_heuristics.prompt_heuristic: Ask which finite claim is honest and which continuum/asymptotic/non-claim boundary remains untouched.
anticipation_heuristics.why_it_matters: Finite support work can be valuable but does not by itself produce continuum, asymptotic, or Clay-level progress.

anticipation_heuristics.pre_cycle_gate: Require a uniform bound ledger or a quarantine decision before promotion.
anticipation_heuristics.prompt_heuristic: Ask which parameter, cutoff, volume, source, or limit must be uniform, and what would falsify uniformity.
anticipation_heuristics.why_it_matters: A bound that is not uniform across the relevant limit can explain local success and global failure at the same time.

anticipation_heuristics.pre_cycle_gate: Reframe or demote until the transfer has independent source and target content.
anticipation_heuristics.prompt_heuristic: Ask whether source and target properties remain independently meaningful after the bridge is removed.
anticipation_heuristics.why_it_matters: A transfer theorem is low value if it defines the target property as the image of the source property.

anticipation_heuristics.pre_cycle_gate: Block ordinary proof search until a falsifier or artifact sprint exists.
anticipation_heuristics.prompt_heuristic: Ask for the cheapest pass/fail test whose failure changes the route state.
anticipation_heuristics.why_it_matters: A hypothesis that cannot fail will usually keep generating plausible but non-decisive cycles.

anticipation_heuristics.pre_cycle_gate: Do not invest ordinary cycles unless the major-publication gate is invest_high_physics_reward.
anticipation_heuristics.prompt_heuristic: Ask what a field reader would understand differently if this succeeds, and whether that difference is publication-weighty.
anticipation_heuristics.why_it_matters: A correct lemma can still be a poor investment if it cannot change field understanding or support a major paper.

anticipation_heuristics.pre_cycle_gate: Route to artifact_sprint, falsifier_sprint, publication_demotion, or quarantine.
anticipation_heuristics.prompt_heuristic: Ask whether the next cycle changes the blocker type, produces the missing artifact, or only rephrases the same obligation.
anticipation_heuristics.why_it_matters: Repeating the same blocker means the branch has stopped learning unless the next cycle produces the named artifact or a new representation.

anticipation_heuristics.pre_cycle_gate: Reframe or quarantine until the physical carrier is named.
anticipation_heuristics.prompt_heuristic: Ask which gauge-invariant observable, Schwinger family, OS Hilbert object, spectral object, or cumulant witness carries the claim.
anticipation_heuristics.why_it_matters: YM work without a physical carrier can drift into mathematically tidy but physically irrelevant estimates.

anticipation_heuristics.pre_cycle_gate: Require limit-order assumptions and a falsifier before claiming physics relevance.
anticipation_heuristics.prompt_heuristic: Ask for an order-of-limits ledger and the first limit where the carrier might disappear.
anticipation_heuristics.why_it_matters: YM routes often fail because local regulator arguments do not commute with continuum, volume, or reconstruction limits.

failure_summary: The route became artifact-bound: the next proof move depends on missing tables, intervals, tails, source data, or explicit certificates.

mathematical_hardness: Positivity is fragile under projection, Schur/Feshbach reduction, closure topology, endpoint singular terms, and source aggregation.
The decisive sign or transfer claim depends on interval arithmetic and uniform tail bounds, so qualitative reasoning cannot close the gate.
Source-derivative data are high-order and equivalence-class dependent; the proof needs exact objects, not narrative source geometry.
Bridge theorems risk circularity unless source and target properties remain independently meaningful.
physics_hardness: Same-theory transfer is hard because the carrier must survive without changing regulator, observable algebra, boundary sector, or normalization.
The route must connect gauge-invariant Euclidean observables to OS/Wightman reconstruction or spectral data without smuggling in a proxy object.
Cutoff, volume, and regulator limits are not passive bookkeeping; they can destroy local positivity, cumulant witnesses, or spectral carriers.
Nontriviality has to be carried by a same-theory observable witness, not by formal nonzero terms in a changed or fixed-regulator model.
representation_hardness: The failed cycles exposed a representation-fit problem: some carriers were too coarse to decide the gate, while raw local objects were too fragmented to transfer.
The efficient representation must encode endpoint/source equivalence classes and aggregate before clipping; otherwise the sign problem is mislocalized.

learning_for_future_cycles: Before investing in a hypothesis, ask for the earliest artifact or falsifier that could have revealed this failure.
Treat repeated blockers as evidence that the branch needs artifact sprint, falsifier sprint, demotion, or quarantine.
Separate hard-but-live proof debt from low-learning repetition by requiring new object-level information at each major cycle set.
required_workflow_change: Attach failure_archaeology after every failed major cycle set.
Run failed-hypothesis-anticipator before ordinary proof search on any branch emerging from a failed set.
Expose the disposition in reports and queue selection before another marathon.

why_failed: The route became artifact-bound: the next proof move depends on missing tables, intervals, tails, source data, or explicit certificates.
why_not_anticipated: Local progress can hide global fragility: each cycle may sharpen a lemma while delaying the artifact or transfer condition that actually decides the route.
The workflow previously asked whether the branch was target-linked, but not always whether the precise missing artifact was already visible before the cycle began.
A successful representation can be misleading when it explains the obstruction after the fact but does not expose the earliest cheap falsifier before investment.
In YM, finite Wilson/OS vocabulary can look physically promising before same-theory carrier survival, cutoff-uniformity, and continuum/spectral gates are separately certified.
